title: harness init: where skills go, every job's default installed, and the preflight on picks
description:
Per the map ticket 'Third-party skills' (harness-0sx.7, Jobs and defaults, Location).

init asks where skills go: this checkout, uncommitted (the default: files in .harness/skills, linked into each Ticket worktree's .claude/skills and .agents/skills when prepare_worktree creates it, hidden through the repo's .git/info/exclude, and into the Review's Run directory); the repo, committed (.agents/skills with .claude/skills links, as today; you commit); or user level (~/.agents/skills, linked from ~/.claude/skills). Non-interactive init takes the default. The choice covers the Shipped skills too (the Stage skills and create-pr); a repo that already committed them in .agents/skills keeps those. Re-running init asks again with the current location as the default answer and moves the Harness-installed skills. attempt() reads the Stage skill from wherever it is, not a fixed .agents/skills.

init installs every job's default (Ticket 17), pinned by commit, even when the skill is already there at user level or through a plugin; in user-level mode it skips a skill you already have there rather than overwrite yours.

Preflight fails when a job's pick is missing, naming the job and the fix ('the self review skill code-review is missing: harness init installs it, or /config picks another'); none opts a job out. It warns when a personal copy shadows an installed skill on Claude (Claude Code runs a personal skill over a project one of the same name), and when the superpowers Claude Code plugin is enabled (its SessionStart hook can stall Stages).

The reasoning behind each decision is on the map's closed tickets: bd show harness-0sx.<n> --json --include-comments. Research notes and prototypes live on local branches: git show research/<name>:docs/research/<file>.md, git show prototype/<name>:<path>. Vocabulary: CONTEXT.md. Decisions: docs/adr/. Rust; crates limited to serde, serde_json, regex, chrono, crossterm, ratatui and ureq, anything else needs a ticket.
acceptance_criteria: init tests with scripted input: each location writes where it says (a temp HOME for user level); non-interactive takes the default; re-running with another answer moves the installed skills and updates the manifest; a user-level copy of yours is not overwritten; the defaults come through a fake git clone; a prepared worktree gets the links and the exclude line. Preflight: a missing pick fails naming its job, none passes, a shadowing personal copy and an enabled superpowers plugin (fake claude plugin list) warn.
